items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: And there was a fellow, they called him Pick, he used to play guitar with my daddy.

ctx.x: Frank Toast, he played with my daddy. And there was a fellow, they called him Pick, he used to play guitar with my daddy. And Selby Thomas, he was a bass player from the day. See, my daddy, my daddy was playing violin and he had this fellow Selby Thomas. And Selby Thomas, he was playing bass. And, oh, they had another other brother, he used to call him William Alonso. He was a trumpet player. But this little brother, he used to get to high all the time and my daddy, he just got disgusted. And that's when he began…
But he didn't go wrong with Tom Alvitt.

items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: So Piggy. So Piggy, he played with me that night

ctx.x: We sure miss out of good times. Old man, Carl, that had his, uh, Royalty place out here. He lived at number 19, uh, or something out here, right off of the Main Street. Right off of Carrollton Avenue, in other words. And, uh... Audubon Street. Audubon Place. That's right here. No, not our town. Yeah. That's back here, right up in Carrollton. You take Alleen Street, or Rename Street, and you go back. Take Alleen Street, and the first street you get after you cross Carrollton Avenue. They got a little street that…
